projects.title: Lend A Hand
projects.description: My friend and I created this project to address an ever-growing problem within the homeless community. Hygiene has and continues to be a problem, especially with homeless teenage girls. We wanted to aid in addressing and helping to reduce the impacts of this problem. To do so, we held an event to collect donations of hygiene products as well as money and educate the general public about this problem. Using the money we collected from ticket sales for this event as well as donations, we were able to purchase additional hygiene products. We held an additional event in which we invited younger Girl Scout troops and taught them how to create feminine hygiene kits with the products we bought and collected. We partnered with a local organization called Friends of Youth to identify the specific products needed and distributed the completed kits. In total, we were able to make and distribute over 300 feminine hygiene kits and taught younger Girl Scout troops how to continue this project in the future. This project allowed us to earn our Silver Award as a part of the Girl Scouts Organization.

I’m officially an O-1 visa holder 🇺🇸 At 18, I left everything in Kyrgyzstan and came to the U.S. for University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign . Growing up in Kyrgyzstan, the odds were stacked against me: I lived in a country where the concept of startups barely existed. People I respected told me that building a company was an impossible dream – especially as a woman. Didn’t have the network, safety net, with only $1500 in my pocket. So I moved 6,000 miles from home. Alone, at 18, to a country where I knew almost no one. At college, I chased down every opportunity I could find, like building one of the largest startup communities on campus and interning at various startups to learn how companies actually get built. The biggest turning point - Afore Capital funded me to move to SF as a Founder in Residence. I met my co-founder Rebecca Wang there, and we started Human Delta to change what AI adoption means for America’s most iconic companies. Since last fall, we: - Assembled an elite engineering team — and we’re expanding fast (we’re hiring!) - Landed Fortune 50 customers, like The Walt Disney Company and ESPN - Raised our round and partnered with Tier 1 investors We are building the missing layer for safe and successful AI adoption, starting with data and knowledge foundation. At 21 years old, I’m finally able to call myself an extraordinary alien building in Silicon Valley with the best team I could ask for. Turns out the dream wasn't impossible. And we’re just getting started. ...more ...more

TLDR: Super excited to officially launch Cura in beta today! Cura is your favorite VCs' AI portfolio analyst. We help GPs, platform leaders, and fund operators keep up to date with everything happening in their portfolio, all in one spot. The best part -> Cura lives in Slack, iMessage, etc. so you don't need to leave your flow of work, and can message Cura like you'd message someone on your team. We're onboarding a few more firms in the coming weeks. DM if interested in giving it a spin! ------- 6 months ago, a few of our VC partners started asking for help managing their portfolio. So I talked to ~150 VCs. Almost everyone had the same problem: There is no central spot for ALL the information about your portfolio. Some of it's in Airtable, some in iMessage threads, some in Slack, some buried in board decks, and email updates. When you need an answer, you're digging through five tools and most of the time not finding what you wanted. And as a result, there's no way to action all that valuable information to best support your portfolio companies. So we built Cura ! Cura is your always-on AI portfolio analyst. It reads LinkedIn, Twitter, news, and websites across your portfolio. It reads and structures board decks, P&Ls, email updates, Granola notes, even iMessage threads. And then it puts it all in one place. The best part: Cura isn't just another dashboard. It lives where you already work, in Slack, email, and iMessage. LP asks about a portco during your quarterly coffee meeting? Text or Slack Cura and get an instant answer. Meet a great candidate but don't know which company needs them? Slack Cura. It pulls open roles and hiring plans from board decks so you know exactly who's hiring for what and when. Early beta funds are loving Cura, and we’re looking to bring in a few more select funds this quarter. DM me if you're tired of digging through five tools to answer a simple question about your own portfolio! ...more ...more

Big update: I dropped out of Stanford! At Stanford, I saw firsthand how fast Al is moving. But I also saw the widening gap between what Al can do and what enterprises are actually ready for. Every company is racing to deploy Al. But there's a problem few talk about: enterprise data — what AI relies on to power decisions and answer questions — is often fragmented, contradictory, and outdated. And AI doesn’t fix bad data. It amplifies it. That’s legal risk, customer churn, and stalled launches waiting to happen. Human Delta is the trust layer between enterprise data and Al tooling: We audit, remediate, and govern the knowledge Al depends on so it can operate with structured, production-grade context. I'm thrilled to be building alongside my best friend and co-founder Akylai Kasymkulova . Since last fall, we've: - Landed contracts with major enterprises like The Walt Disney Company (and others to be announced soon) - Built an exceptional team in San Francisco - Raised millions in a round led by Susa Ventures and Wischoff Ventures If you’re looking to deploy AI tools safely and at scale at your company, I'd love to connect. P.S. We’re scaling fast across engineering and GTM teams to keep up with customer growth. Email rebecca@humandelta.ai if interested ...more ...more

Last month, we took on 6 new clients. The past couple weeks we've taken zero. Here's what's top of mind in Month 2 of Sapience : 1. Selling can be a drug - know when to stop As we started to get revenue momentum, there's been pull to stack more. But after closing a few deals, we quickly realized our ops could be more polished. So, we halted sales to prioritize customer experience. 2. Prioritize love of the game over short-term cash My 30 minute morning slots can either be sales calls or reading new research on seo/aeo. For any long term game, the latter is more important. 3. Don't let last week's priorities dictate today's actions. In any early-stage business/startup, the constraint changes every week. Two weeks ago, my inner dialogue was “how do we get customers," now it's "how can we attribute revenue at close certainty” 4. Don't hide behind vanity metrics Especially in seo/aeo, it's easy to point to "impressions" and "clicks" making an impact. In reality, conversions & attributable ROI are what create long term value - how do we prioritize the latter. More exciting updates coming soon
